model_reported.summary: Proposed a single row-granularity scheduling change while retaining the scalar recurrence and coordinate expressions.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: Used the supplied target/compiler context; the proposal requires no hardware-specific assumptions or ISA changes.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The candidate uses a basic OpenMP parallel-for schedule and num_threads clause; no uncertain API or hardware property motivates a documentation request.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Recorded the measured serial baseline as context only and left correctness and performance evaluation to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a baseline comparator; it does not establish one- versus four-thread performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied serial baseline was correct on its eight reported cases and had a mean runtime of about 0.56342 seconds across three samples; the observations do not separate one- and four-thread timings.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this dynamic-row candidate at one and four threads, including n=1024 and shifted-bound cases.

proposal.hypothesis: Dynamic scheduling of one complete row at a time may reduce imbalance from rows with different Mandelbrot iteration counts compared with contiguous static row allocation. The serial branch avoids OpenMP overhead when the usable team is one; capping the team by height avoids requesting workers that cannot receive rows. The recurrence and per-pixel coordinate expressions remain unchanged.

retained: Parallelize the outer row loop with OpenMP dynamic scheduling and chunk size one when the usable team has more than one thread.
Keep a serial nested-loop path for a one-thread usable team and cap the requested team size at the number of rows.
